clue.text: Pacts between witches and social workers

parts.note: a coven is a gathering of witches
ants are social insects whose colonies are full of tireless workers

explanation.surface: Agreements struck between a gathering of witches and the local social services team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Social workers' looks like council staff, but it means ANTS, insects living in organised colonies; 'between' just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Covenants are formal agreements or binding promises, so they are synonyms for pacts.

clue.text: A serving man needing such punishment?

definitions.text: A serving man needing such punishment?

parts.words: A serving man needing such punishment?
parts.note: a soldier in service holding a junior rank whose title is also the word for physical punishment of the body, as in caning

explanation.definitionFit: A corporal is a non-commissioned army rank, and corporal punishment is beating.

clue.text: In high spirits, a shout of "long live the Manchester team!"

parts.note: viva is the Italian cry meaning 'long live!'
Manchester City is a Premier League football club

explanation.surface: Elated football fans cheer for their Manchester club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a shout of' frames VIVA as a cry; the team is Manchester City, the football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Vivacity is liveliness and animation, the quality of being full of energy.

clue.text: Fighters who turn turtle?

parts.note: not capsizing but becoming turtles, as the cartoon Teenage Mutant heroes are reptile warriors trained in Japanese martial arts

explanation.definitionFit: Ninjas are Japanese covert warriors, famed through the cartoon heroes who are turtles.

clue.text: Require the French to give a pointer

parts.note: to need is to require
le is the masculine form of 'the' in French

explanation.surface: A demand that the French should supply some directions.
explanation.definitionFit: A needle is the indicator on a dial or compass, which points.

clue.text: It's over a foot long in skeleton

definitions.text: It's over a foot long in skeleton

parts.words: It's over a foot long in skeleton
parts.note: a long bone of the lower leg sitting above the foot, and indeed over twelve inches in length

explanation.definitionFit: The shinbone, or tibia, is the leg bone running from knee to ankle above the foot.

clue.text: Setback for graduate's friends

parts.note: an MA, Master of Arts, is a university graduate

indicators.note: back, inside the word Setback, tells us the word set that comes before it is read backwards

parts.note: the opening letters of Setback taken as written

explanation.surface: A newly qualified student finds their friends have become a hindrance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setback' is split: 'back' turns SET into TES, which follows MA.
explanation.definitionFit: Mates is the everyday British word for pals or companions.

clue.text: Mother getting hot with an Indian aristocrat — and another one!

parts.note: ma is a familiar word for mother
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
the indefinite article, giving A
a raja is an Indian prince or king

explanation.surface: A mother takes up with a fiery Indian noble, and then a second.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition 'another one!' refers back to 'Indian aristocrat': the answer is a grander Indian prince.
explanation.definitionFit: A maharaja is a great Indian prince, the higher rank of the same title.

clue.text: Turin, as the locals know it

definitions.text: Turin, as the locals know it

parts.words: Turin, as the locals know it
parts.note: the Piedmontese city under its own Italian name rather than the English form

explanation.definitionFit: Torino is the Italian name of the city of Turin in Piedmont.

clue.text: Glows like black eyes — run out!

indicators.note: out says the abbreviation for run is removed from the word for black eyes

parts.note: shiners is slang for black eyes
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: A warning to flee from someone with bruised eyes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'run out' looks like a cricket dismissal, but 'out' removes R (run) from SHINERS.
explanation.definitionFit: To shine is to give off light, so it glows.

clue.text: Green veg not quite cooked — a dish best served cold

indicators.note: food that is cooked has been worked over and changed, so the letters before it are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written as part of the letters to be mixed

indicators.note: not quite the whole word, so veg loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A kitchen note about vegetables left underdone and served cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not quite' trims VEG to VE; 'cooked' then rearranges GREEN plus VE. The definition is the proverb 'revenge is a dish best served cold'.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says vengeance is sweetest when taken calmly long after the wrong, hence a cold dish.

clue.text: Tooth-like projection, found in hollow, to make a note on

parts.note: a dent is a hollow or depression in a surface
ti (or te) is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone spots a toothy bump in a hollow and jots a note about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' and 'to make' are link words; the pieces DENT, A, TI and ON simply follow one another.
explanation.definitionFit: Dentation is a toothed edge or a tooth-shaped point, as on a serrated leaf margin.

clue.text: Energy user is about to publish again

indicators.note: about here means moved around, so the letters of the pieces before it are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
E is the standard symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: A power consumer is on the verge of putting something out again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'on the point of', but it is the anagram signal for E + USER + IS.
explanation.definitionFit: A reissue is a fresh release of something already printed or recorded, so to reissue is to bring it out a second time.

clue.text: Loudspeakers?

parts.note: read not as audio equipment but as people who speak loudly in public, delivering addresses to a crowd

explanation.definitionFit: Orators are public speakers who declaim to audiences, playfully called loud speakers.

clue.text: Setting out, as the waiter does every day

definitions.text: Setting out, as the waiter does every day

parts.words: Setting out, as the waiter does every day
parts.note: a waiter's daily routine includes setting out cutlery and cloths before service, and the phrase also means displaying or presenting

explanation.definitionFit: To lay the table is to set out plates and cutlery, the restaurant routine each morning.

clue.text: Annoyance expressed in an EC-us renegotiation

indicators.note: a renegotiation reworks the terms, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Irritation at a trade deal being renegotiated between Europe and America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'renegotiation' rearranges the letters of IN AN ECUS; 'expressed' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuisance is something that annoys or causes bother.

clue.text: Fixed time to re-site destructive insects

parts.note: a term is a fixed period of time, such as a school term

indicators.note: re- as in re-site signals that the word site that follows is laid out afresh, rearranged

explanation.surface: A fixed time is set for moving damaging bugs elsewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 're-site' is split: 're-' rearranges SITE to ITES, which follows TERM.
explanation.definitionFit: Termites are wood-eating insects that do great damage to timber in buildings.

clue.text: Omit to put dustbins in place?

definitions.meaning: playfully, to set the bins outside the house for the rubbish collection

explanation.definitionFit: Both readings fit the phrase: to exclude or skip, and literally to place the bins outdoors for the refuse lorry.

clue.text: Riot rosy organised in American society

indicators.note: organised means arranged into order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rowdy, rose-tinted riot is staged at an American college club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organised' rearranges RIOT ROSY; 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A sorority is a women's student society at an American college.

clue.text: A more frightening sign of injury? That's right

parts.note: a scar is the mark left by a healed wound
i.e., id est, means 'that is'

explanation.surface: Someone sees a wound's mark as more alarming, and is told they're correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's' gives IE, the abbreviation of id est, 'that is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarier is the comparative of scary, so it means causing greater fear.

clue.text: The following moment

definitions.meaning: the next in order after the first
a very short span of time, as in 'wait a sec'

explanation.definitionFit: Second means next in sequence after the first, and also a brief instant of time.

clue.text: A radical way to describe acid

definitions.meaning: a chemical group acting as a unit in compounds
the word prefixes the name of an acid, as in acetylsalicylic acid, which is aspirin

explanation.definitionFit: Acetyl is a chemical group derived from acetic acid, and it names aspirin's acetylsalicylic acid.

clue.text: Pirate with a rude manner of speaking

indicators.note: manner of speaking says the words are taken as they are spoken, by their sound

parts.note: rude means coarse and a manner is an air, giving coarse air

explanation.surface: A buccaneer who talks with crude, uncouth bluster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manner of speaking' looks like a description of the pirate's talk; 'of speaking' tells you to say 'coarse air' out loud.
explanation.definitionFit: A corsair was a privateer or raider of the Mediterranean, a sea robber.

clue.text: Move quickly to bury, perhaps

definitions.meaning: to go at a horse's easy gallop
the word that comes before bury to make the Kent cathedral city

explanation.definitionFit: A canter is a horse's three-beat pace, and canter followed by bury gives Canterbury, the cathedral city in Kent.

clue.text: Clergyman is English and must study again

parts.note: Rev, short for Reverend, is the title of a clergyman

explanation.surface: A vicar who is English has to go back to his books.
explanation.definitionFit: To revise is to go over material again before an exam.

clue.text: A thousand in formation, going for a burn-up

indicators.note: in tells us the thousand goes inside the word for formation

parts.note: creation is the act of forming or bringing into being
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: A thousand aircraft fly in formation, heading for a fiery climax.
explanation.definitionFit: Cremation is the burning of a body, so a dead person's last trip goes to the burn-up.

clue.text: 3 X e, a sound format in north Africa

indicators.note: a sound format suggests a version for the ear, so the expression is pronounced, not read

parts.note: three times e, said out loud, is triple e

explanation.surface: A technical label for an audio standard used across north Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: Say 'triple E' (3 times E) quickly and it sounds like the Libyan capital. The definition is loose: a place found in north Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripoli is the capital of Libya, on the north African coast.

clue.text: Dig in, like Derek trotter on the big day

parts.note: Derek Trotter, Del Boy, is the market trader in the British sitcom Only Fools and Horses
VE Day, Victory in Europe Day on 8 May 1945, was the big day of celebration

explanation.surface: Someone tucks in to a feast, like a TV wide boy at a wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: Derek Trotter is known as Del Boy in the British sitcom Only Fools and Horses; 'the big day' is not a wedding but VE (Victory in Europe) Day.
explanation.definitionFit: To delve is to dig or burrow, literally or into a subject.

clue.text: Snakes found by sentry, before retreating inside!

indicators.note: inside places the turned word within the word sentry

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the word for before is reversed

parts.note: pre- is a prefix meaning before

explanation.surface: A guard discovers snakes and then backs off indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreating' turns PRE into ERP, which 'inside' puts after the S of SENTRY.
explanation.definitionFit: Serpentry is a collective term for serpents, a gathering of reptiles.
